name: Southern banana pudding
description: Old-fashioned banana pudding: stovetop vanilla custard over wafers and bananas, under a toasted meringue.

ingredients.name: egg yolks (save the whites for the meringue)
medium bananas, sliced ½ inch thick

steps: Whisk the [sugar](@sugar), [flour](@flour) and [salt](@salt) in a medium bowl. Whisk in [½ cup of the milk](@milk:0.5) and the [egg yolks](@egg-yolks).
Heat the [rest of the milk](@milk:3) in a large saucepan over medium heat until it simmers.
Slowly whisk about a third of the hot milk into the egg mixture to warm it, then whisk it all back into the saucepan.
Bring it to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly, and cook about 3 minutes more, until thick.
Take it off the heat and stir in the [butter](@butter) and [vanilla](@vanilla) until the butter melts. Let it cool slightly.
Cover the bottom of a 9 by 13 inch baking dish with [vanilla wafers](@wafers), keeping a few back for the top if you like. Layer the [banana slices](@bananas) over them.
Pour the pudding through a fine-mesh sieve over the bananas and spread it evenly.
Beat the [egg whites](@egg-whites) and [cream of tartar](@cream-of-tartar) on high until soft peaks form. Add the [sugar](@meringue-sugar) a little at a time and beat to stiff peaks.
Spread the meringue over the pudding all the way to the edges of the dish.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes, until the meringue is lightly browned. Top with the saved wafers if you like, and let it cool 10 minutes before serving.
tips: Use bananas that are ripe but not very ripe. Very ripe ones break down too much in the oven.
The wafers are one 11 oz box per batch.
